claims.text: Adding 10–30 vol% SiC to ZrB2 and reactively hot pressing it below 1700 °C will improve sinterability.
The ZrB2–SiC composite will have better oxidation resistance than single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The ZrB2–SiC composite will have better liquid plating-metal corrosion durability than single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Reactive hot pressing at 1600–1700 °C under an inert atmosphere is an applicable preparation route for the proposed composite.
The proposed composite is applicable in air at 1200–1500 °C.
The proposed composite is applicable in molten Cu or Ni at 1200–1400 °C.
Processing will form a ZrB2–SiC composite microstructure with SiC distributed at grain boundaries.
SiC acts as a sintering aid in ZrB2.
SiC reduces grain growth and porosity during processing.
SiC produces a protective SiO2-rich glassy layer during oxidation.
SiC acts as a barrier to liquid-metal infiltration and corrosion.
The composite will achieve greater than 95% density.
The composite will achieve flexural strength greater than 400 MPa.
The composite will exhibit oxidation mass gain below 0.1 mg/cm² after 10 hours in air at 1300 °C.
The composite will exhibit liquid-metal corrosion weight loss below 0.05 mg/cm²/h.
Single-phase ZrB2 prepared above 2300 °C has high density, strength, and oxidation resistance.
Preparing single-phase ZrB2 above 2300 °C is impractical.
ZrB2 prepared below 1700 °C has lower density and strength and poor oxidation and corrosion resistance.
The magnitude of improvement depends on SiC content and processing parameters.
Performance is not established outside 10–30 vol% SiC or above 1500 °C.

contradictions.description: The intervention is repeatedly specified as occurring below 1700 °C, but the preparation and experiment ranges include 1700 °C.
The conditions limit liquid plating-metal service to 1200–1400 °C, whereas the boundary states that both air and liquid-bath testing apply through 1500 °C.
